title: Self-Supervised Adaptation of Dense DINOv3 Features for Improved In-Context Vegetation Segmentation
abstract: Dense vegetation segmentation must transfer across fields, crops, viewpoints, and sensing platforms, but dense annotation for every condition is costly. In-context segmentation instead transfers a reference vegetation mask without task-specific segmentation training, placing strong demands on dense features: they must retain local detail for intra-crop transfer while tolerating cross-crop and cross-source appearance changes. We study this trade-off in DINOv3 features for agricultural imagery. DINOv3-L provides strong local specificity but can be overly appearance-specific across crops, whereas DINOv3-S yields a more tolerant similarity structure. We therefore train a lightweight residual adapter on frozen DINOv3-L features, using frozen DINOv3-S features to filter potential false negatives. On the Agroscapes dataset, within a fixed in-context segmentation pipeline, the adapted representation improves transfer within and across crops and between aerial and ground-based sources.
